VERDICT: EXTEND C0031 | `evaluate_fix()` treats tool-runner failures as zero issues because `_count_tool_issues()` catches all exceptions and returns 0, but runner non-exception failure paths also collapse to 0: `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="NOT_FOUND"|"TIMEOUT")`, runners mostly return `[]`, and `_count_tool_issues()` converts that to count 0. FOLLOW: a missing/timed-out pyright/ruff/bandit run on the patched sandbox can make a broken fix look unchanged or improved, so `_compute_fix_verdict()` can emit SAFE/NEUTRAL without any real post-fix analysis. This directly contaminates Stage 4 in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, where SAFE/NEUTRAL marks findings `verified=True`, activating the bug-closed gate and suppressing future reports. The simplest sufficient fix is stronger than “high penalty on exception” alone: treat any runner execution failure (exception, NOT_FOUND, TIMEOUT, parse failure) as UNEVALUABLE for the whole fix evaluation instead of 0 issues.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox the source tree correctly for tests. It writes only the patched target file into a temp directory (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs `test_cmd` with `cwd=tmpdir`, but it does not copy the rest of the repository, adjust import paths, or rewrite file arguments inside `test_cmd`. Evidence from the code: the tempdir contains just one file; `test_cmd` is executed verbatim; the advertised contract says “sandbox-test proposed fixes” and “never modifies actual source”, but the executed tests are not actually pointed at a full sandboxed project. In the real caller, `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", "-x", "-q", "--tb=no", "--no-header", "-q"]`; from inside the tempdir that path usually does not exist, and even if tests discover project files via sys.path, they will import the real repo, not the patched sandbox copy.
FOLLOW: This breaks the key new capability. The fix-evaluation stage can report `tests_passed=False` for environmental reasons unrelated to the patch, causing good fixes to be marked HARMFUL, or it can run against the real source tree and completely miss regressions in the patched file, causing bad fixes to be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL. Downstream, `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` uses SAFE/NEUTRAL to set `finding.verified = True`, which closes bugs in NK dedup and suppresses further review. Because the sandbox is not a real sandboxed project, the verified flag can be wrong in either direction, directly affecting registry quality and end-to-end behavior.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when evaluating a fix, copy the whole relevant source tree into the tempdir, preserve the target file’s relative path inside that tree, write the patched file there, and run tests/tooling against that copied tree (same relative paths, `cwd` set to sandbox root). Do not run tests from a tempdir containing only the basename of the patched file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as SAFE when one tool gets worse and another improves more, because it sums net deltas across tool classes: `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; if `total_net < 0`, verdict is SAFE. Example from the code’s own arithmetic: a fix that introduces +1 bandit security issue but removes -2 ruff issues yields `total_net = -1`, therefore SAFE. That contradicts the documented meaning “SAFE: no new issues introduced”.
FOLLOW: This is a silently wrong result in the fix-evaluation pipeline. A harmful regression in security or typing can be masked by unrelated lint reductions and then propagated as SAFE. Downstream, Stage 4 in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` marks SAFE or NEUTRAL findings as `verified=True`, so a fix that introduced a real new issue can still close the bug and activate NK’s bug-closed gate. That degrades both the endocrine module’s own verdict quality and the larger immune/insect-brain workflow.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute HARMFUL if any individual net metric is positive (`net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`); compute SAFE only if at least one metric improved and none worsened; otherwise keep the existing NEUTRAL/tests logic.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `health_trend()` is structurally incompatible with its own contract “diagnostic count trends across rounds (by category)” because it only appends counts for categories present in each scan: `for cat, count in scan.counts_by_category.items(): trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. Registry findings C0002/C0006 already cover omitted zero-count rounds for categories that disappear. This method has a second, separate interface bug: categories that appear for the first time in later rounds get shorter histories starting mid-series, so the returned lists are not aligned to round indices at all. Example: if category A first appears in round 3, `trend["A"] == [count_round_3]`, which the caller cannot map onto full round history without extra reconstruction.
FOLLOW: Any consumer treating index `i` as round `i` gets wrong trends, even if it handles “missing zero” for existing categories. This can mislead any future trend-based pacing or health regression logic in the insect brain by shifting late-appearing categories earlier in time. Because the method advertises round trends, this is a silent interface error, not mere formatting.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — build trends over the full union of categories across all scans and emit one entry per scan in round order for every category, using `0` when absent. That simultaneously fixes missing-zero and late-category misalignment.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can choose the wrong file by substring match: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path: return sp_path`. The fallback `match in sp_path` is too loose. A description mentioning `brain.py` can match an unrelated path containing that substring, and any short relative fragment can bind to the first containing path rather than the intended file. This is especially fragile because it concatenates `finding.description + " " + finding.proposed_fix`, so arbitrary prose in the proposed fix participates in file selection.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can patch and analyze the wrong file while still returning a concrete verdict. That makes SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL silently meaningless for the intended finding. Downstream, the immune pipeline may mark the finding verified based on analysis of the wrong file, closing the wrong bug and suppressing valid future findings.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — restrict matching to exact normalized basename or exact suffix path-segment matches from extracted `.py` paths; remove the generic `match in sp_path` substring fallback.
VERIFIED: TRUE

CONFIRM C0029

CONFIRM C0031

EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` not only marks missing tools as available; parse failures are also treated as availability. Each runner returns `[]` on JSON/regex parse failure after logging a warning, and `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally. FOLLOW: a tool can be installed, invoked, and produce unusable output, yet the health report still claims that the tool is available and contributes zero diagnostics. This creates the same false-clean health scan as missing binaries and also masks parser regressions. The same explicit execution-status propagation fix should distinguish at least AVAILABLE_OK, AVAILABLE_UNPARSEABLE, and UNAVAILABLE.

EXTEND C0021 | The timeout handling bug is more severe in fix evaluation than in health scanning. FOLLOW: when a post-fix tool run times out, the runner returns `[]`, `_count_tool_issues()` reads that as zero issues, and `_compute_fix_verdict()` may upgrade the fix to SAFE/NEUTRAL. This can set `verified=True` in the immune pipeline and prematurely close the bug. The fix should cover both scan and fix-evaluation paths, not just `scan_health()`.
